regions.region: title, abstract, and introduction across the original page
regions.finding: The abstract summarizes the paper's Ru/Os allyl and vinyl outcomes. These statements were merged as cross-page evidence into the later equation records; no duplicate abstract-only experiment was created. The introduction gives broad cited context but no row-level present-paper experiment or reaction arrow on this page.

unresolved: Abstract-level statements do not supply quantities, conditions, yields, or complete structures beyond the formulas shown in text.
Broad metal/R lists in the introduction were not expanded into unsupported individual literature experiments.

regions.finding: Equation 1 is a generic allene-insertion scheme with allyl and vinyl alternatives, not an executed experiment. Three explicit rare prior-work reactions in the prose and three previously reported Ru/CO allene cases were classified as literature examples.
X-ray structures of present-paper products 2 and 4 were linked to equation 2 and the phenyl case of equation 3; the figures were not counted as separate reactions.
The page introduces the hydride systems and identifies some Ru/CO reactions as previously reported; detailed present-paper equations continue on later pages.

unresolved: Prior-work prose omits quantities, conditions, yields, and, for the Zr mixture, individual product structures and ratio.
The compact Erker product formula requires review against the cited source before assigning connectivity.

regions.region: lower-left equation 2 and Results and Discussion text
regions.finding: One present-paper insertion of RuHCl(CO)(PPh3)3 with methyl buta-2,3-dienoate was extracted, giving allyl complex 2; NMR and X-ray confirmation were associated with the same record.
These are crystallographic/refinement and bond-geometry tables for products 2 and 4, not reaction-condition tables; no additional experiment records were created.
The top completes the citation to prior Os/PPh3 vinyl-complex work; the lower-right introduces the present OsHCl(CO)(PPh3)3 phenylallene case that is drawn as equation 3 on page 4.

unresolved: Equation 2 on pages 1-6 omits quantities, solvent, time, temperature, atmosphere, workup, purification, and yield.
Crystallographic data establish structure but do not provide a separate synthesis condition.

regions.region: upper-left equation 3 and adjacent product discussion
regions.finding: The shared equation-3 arrow was split into two present-paper substrate cases (R = Ph and CH2Ph), producing allyl complexes 4 and 5. Table 3 is bond geometry for 4 and was not treated as another reaction.
The three R cases (CMe3, Ph, CO2Et) were classified as separate literature examples because the authors explicitly say they were shown previously in reference 20.

One present-paper RuHCl(PPh3)3/4,4-dimethyl-1,2-pentadiene reaction giving vinyl complex 11 was extracted. Two additional present-paper reactions with phenylallene and ethyl allenoate were retained separately as unsuccessful/indeterminate mixtures.

unresolved: Pages 1-6 omit full reaction quantities, conditions, yields, workups, and purifications for equations 3 and 5.
The two mixture-producing reactions do not identify or quantify individual products.
Complex organometallic connectivity was not converted to SMILES.

regions.finding: Scheme 1 is a DFT model network, split into PC1 (tris-phosphine model) and PC2 (carbonyl/phosphine model) mechanism records. Its branch arrows are mechanistic alternatives, not wet experiments.
The first sentence completes the NMR comparison for product 11 and was merged into the equation-5 record; the remaining text discusses theoretical pathways.
The prose identifies the PC1 vinyl route as kinetically favored and the PC2 allyl route as kinetically and thermodynamically favored; ONIOM is used to assess PPh3 steric effects.

unresolved: Calculated transition-state/intermediate structures were not assigned SMILES.
Scheme 1 contains no experimental quantities, workup, purification, or yield because it is computational.

regions.finding: Calculated PC1 vinyl/allyl energy profiles were associated with the PC1 mechanism record; values are relative free energies with electronic energies in parentheses, not reaction yields.
Calculated PC2 vinyl/allyl profiles, including PH3-model and ONIOM/PPh3 energy sets, were associated with the PC2 mechanism record; no experimental reaction record was created.
The text relates the lower PC2 barriers to weaker back-bonding in the presence of CO and continues onto page 7; page 7 is not claimed as covered.

unresolved: The mechanistic explanation continues beyond the requested page range.
Energy values are retained as source text because kcal/mol is not a supported structured reaction-quantity unit in the current schema.
